reason: Neurologic and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome. Strabismus is frequent (30-79%); microdontia (2/5) and carious teeth (3/5) support dental involvement.
The definition establishes a predominantly cutaneous disorder. Extracutaneous abnormalities are isolated reports; the parent's musculoskeletal label need not be inherited.
Encephalopathy defines the disease. Cleft palate (7/11), contractures (6/11), clubfoot (5/11) and scoliosis (4/11) support direct oral and skeletal involvement above 30%.
Endocrine deficiency and retinal degeneration define the syndrome. Frequent dental abnormalities and very frequent osteoporosis with skeletal maturation defects support the involved organs.
Enchondromatosis and the metabolic abnormality define this syndrome. Neurologic, renal and ocular abnormalities are occasional (5-29%), below the involvement threshold.
The evidence supports a metabolic disorder. Urinary peptide excretion does not establish renal damage; intellectual disability has no frequency sufficient to establish common neurologic involvement.
Ocular, dental and digital defects define the disease. Frequent neurologic impairment merits the fourth axis; the cap permits omission of less consequential hair changes and hearing involvement.

Remove neurologic and otologic: developmental delay and hearing impairment each reported in one patient do not establish intrinsic damage in at least 30% of this KRT5 subtype. Oral blistering in 3/3 supports gastrointestinal involvement.

corrected.basis: KRT5-related skin fragility; oral mucosal blistering in 3/3 supports gastrointestinal involvement. Singleton neurologic, hearing and skeletal findings do not establish common involvement.

reason: Inherited bile-acid handling dysfunction supports gastrointestinal and metabolic primary axes. Liver enzyme abnormalities in 2/2 and periportal fibrosis in 1/2 support direct hepatic involvement.

Remove ocular and gastrointestinal: microphthalmia and microdontia/microglossia in one assessed patient do not establish involvement in at least 30% of this subtype. Microcephalic skeletal dwarfism remains defining.

corrected.basis: Microcephalic primordial skeletal dwarfism defines the subtype. Ocular and oral defects are singleton observations without established >=30% prevalence; renal ectopia is occasional.
